change: Bounded notification signal admission, idle disconnect recovery and exclusive D-Bus name ownership
architecture: Protocol queue, connection lifetime and name acquisition remain in FreedesktopNotifications. NotificationPort and the pure NotificationInbox policy are unchanged. The desktop inspection API exposes notification-history visibility for reversible native checks.
reproductions: With the watch consumer stalled and 256 close signals queued, Notify accepted another request instead of returning overload
Terminating an idle private daemon produced no unavailable update before the three-second test deadline
Default name flags displaced an existing private-bus notification server

private_bus.fixtures: Each protocol test owns a private dbus-daemon and explicit address; no environment mutation selects the desktop bus
adapter_unit_cases: Two-signal rejection and one-slot resident action
Expiration batches defer without losing active notifications
Connection teardown discards pending signals and rejects offline actions

runtime.notes: Native VM checks. Presentation recovery policy is unit-tested; driver fault injection is not covered here.

native.deployment_scope: Desktop executable only; existing lock/login executables were not replaced

limits: The bounded pending queue can coexist with one drained batch; zbus buffers, decoded requests, snapshots and other owners have separate memory costs
Accepted signals are best effort across disconnect; old pending signals are discarded and are not durably replayed
Inbox/history remain in memory; persistence, grouping and rich notifications remain pending
Existing 100 ms watch interval and two-second connection-failure backoff remain; no CPU or memory improvement measurement is claimed
Bus loss and contention were tested only on private daemons; the host and guest desktop buses were not restarted by those fixtures
Native UI tests verify action/dismiss clicks, replacement and expiration; signal protocol semantics have separate private-bus evidence
